newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Tunnel discovered outside Colombian prison.
newsitem.headline: Tunnel discovered outside Colombian prison.

text.p: An 82-foot 25-metre tunnel was discovered on Friday leading from a house to a prison outside Colombia's southwest city of Cali, authorities said.

A statement from the National Penitentiary Institute said a man and a woman caught inside the house, from which the tunnel was being dug toward the Palmira prison, were arrested after its discovery shortly after midday.

The maximum security wing of the prison houses three high-ranking members of Colombia's powerful Cali drug cartel. But authorities said the tunnel was pointed in the direction of a wing housing common criminals.

Officials from the U.S. Bureau of Prisons have been touring Colombia's maximum security prisons since late last month to advise authorities on ways to preventing high-profile escapes like the one involving Cali cartel drug lord Jose Santacruz Londono, which seriously embarrassed the government last year.

Santacruz, the No. 3 man in the cartel, walked out of Bogota's La Picota prison in broad daylight on Jan. 1, 1996. He was gunned down by police outside the northwest city of Medellin two months later.
